question: Deepthi loses Rs. 300 yearly on simple interest when the rate of interest falls from 12(1)/(2)% to 10(1)/(2)%. The amount invested by Deepthi is:
solution:
**Given:**

Rate(r₁) = 12{1over2}%

Rate(r₂) = 10{1over2}%

Time(t) = 1 year

Losses of simple interest yearly = Rs. 300

**Formula used:**

Simple interest = (P × R × T) / 100

**Calculation:**

Let the amount invested by Deepthi be Rs. x.

The rate of interest fall = 12{1over2}% – 10{1over2}%

⇒ (25over2 – 21over2)% = 4over2% = 2%

The rate of interest fall = 2%

Simple interest = (P × R × T) / 100

⇒ 300 = (x× 2× 1)over100 

⇒ 2x = 30000

⇒ x = 30000over2 = Rs. 15000

**∴ The amount invested by Deepthi is Rs. 15,000.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**** **If the rate of interest is fall.

Simple interest = {P × R × (T₁ - T₂)} / 100

⇒ 300 = {x×1times({25over2} - {21over2})}over100 

⇒ 300 = (x× 2× 1)over100 

⇒ x = 30000over2 = Rs. 15000

∴ The amount invested by Deepthi is Rs. 15,000.
